Yıllardır binlerce saatimizi gömdüğümüz, her genişleme paketini desteklediğimiz bir oyunun ve arkasındaki şirketin ulaştığı ikiyüzlülük seviyesi artık görmezden gelinebilecek gibi değil.

Hearts of Iron IV, insanlık tarihinin en kanlı dönemini, 2. Dünya Savaşı’nı merkezine alan bir strateji oyunu. Oyunda 20. yüzyılın en acımasız diktatörleri, milyonlarca insanın ölümünden sorumlu liderleri portreleriyle, odak ağaçlarıyla, alternatif tarih senaryolarıyla yer alıyor; hatta oyuncular bu figürleri dilediğince yönetip fantezilerini gerçekleştirebiliyor. Şirket için bu tarihsel figürler "oyun mekaniği" ve "kazanç kapısı" sayılırken, resmi Discord sunucusunda yaşanan son olay Paradox yönetiminin ve moderasyon ekibinin gerçek zihniyetini açıkça ortaya koydu.

Resmi Discord sunucusunda bir Türk oyuncunun, yalnızca profil fotoğrafında Türkiye Cumhuriyeti’nin kurucusu Mustafa Kemal Atatürk yer aldığı için "tartışmalı figür" bahanesiyle sunucudan banlanması ve üstüne moderatör tarafından asılsız, iftira niteliğinde tarihi suçlamalarda bulunulması tam anlamıyla bir rezalettir.

Mustafa Kemal Atatürk; emperyalizme karşı bağımsızlık savaşı vermiş, modern, laik bir cumhuriyet inşa etmiş, UNESCO tarafından 1981 yılında "Uluslararası anlayış, iş birliği ve barış yolunda çalışmış üstün bir devlet adamı" olarak tescillenmiş dünya çapında bir liderdir. "Yurtta barış, dünyada barış" ilkesini benimsemiş böylesi bir lideri; Hitler’in, Stalin’in, Mussolini’nin ve Mao’nun fink attığı bir oyunun topluluğunda "tartışmalı" ilan edip ban gerekçesi yapmak, tarihi cehaletin ötesinde doğrudan Türklere yönelik ideolojik bir önyargının ve çifte standardın kanıtıdır.

İş Türk oyuncuların cebindeki paraya gelince hiçbir sorun yok:

Battle for the Bosporus DLC'sini çıkarırken Türkiye'yi ve Atatürk’ün mirasını pazarlama malzemesi yapıp satmayı gayet iyi biliyorsunuz.

Türk oyuncu topluluğunun yıllardır oyuna verdiği emeği, desteği ve ilgiyi sömürmeyi gayet iyi biliyorsunuz.

Ama resmi platformlarınızda bu ülkenin kurucusuna iftira atan, kendi siyasi saplantılarını moderatörlük yetkisi arkasına saklayan tiplere yetki verip oyuncuları aşağılamaktan da geri durmuyorsunuz.

Bir strateji oyunu geliştiricisinin moderasyon ekibi, tarihi gerçekleri kendi çarpık ideolojilerine göre eğip bükemez; resmi bir sunucuda bir ulusun kurucu liderine iftira atıp oyuncuları ötekileştiremez.

Paradox Interactive bu moderasyon rezaleti hakkında resmi bir açıklama yapana, ilgili moderatörle yollarını ayırıp Türk oyuncu topluluğundan açıkça özür dileyene kadar bu inceleme burada olumsuz olarak kalacak. Tarih bilmeyen, oyuncusuna ve değerlerine saygı duymayan bir anlayışa ne bir kuruş ne de olumlu bir puan kazandırmak mümkün.

If you are willing to disregard your corporate responsibility at the expense of losing players who have invested hundreds  in some cases thousands of hours into your games, then you risk doing far more than alienating part of your community. You risk undermining the very foundation on which your current and future games depend.
And for what?
To continue protecting a Discord moderator who feels entitled to make sweeping and derogatory statements about the founder of a nation  a historically significant figure widely associated with state-building, modernization, and peace without demonstrating the level of objective, comprehensive historical research that such claims would require?
A community moderator is not merely an individual expressing personal opinions. By holding an official role, that person represents the standards, judgment, and values of the organization that has entrusted them with authority.
That is why the real issue is no longer the moderator’s personal views alone. The real issue is how your company chooses to respond when someone representing your community behaves in a manner that many long-standing players consider disrespectful, provocative, and incompatible with the responsibilities of that position.
What I want to see now is whether your organization has the institutional maturity and self-correcting capacity to recognize a serious mistake and act accordingly.
Will you listen to the players who have supported your games for years, invested substantial amounts of their time in your products, and helped sustain your community?
Or are you prepared to damage that relationship  and potentially lose part of your most dedicated player base simply to defend the conduct of a single Discord moderator?
The answer will say a great deal about how seriously you value your community, your reputation, and the long-term future of your games.

If you develop games such as Hearts of Iron IV, where history and historical figures are central to the experience, I expect the same level of care, consistency, and responsibility from your community moderation.
I find the handling of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk's portrait, and particularly the attempt to associate him with the events of 1915 as part of a moderation justification, deeply unacceptable. Moderators should not turn their own interpretations of highly serious and disputed historical matters into grounds for moderation.
What makes this worse is that Paradox itself subsequently acknowledged that its rules concerning profile pictures of real people had not been applied consistently. If a community rule exists, it should be enforced according to the same standards regardless of the historical figure involved. Selective or inconsistent enforcement damages the community's trust in the moderation system.
I acknowledge that Paradox has since stated that the matter is being reviewed. However, for me, this is about more than a Discord moderation decision. A company that creates historically focused games for an international audience should ensure that its community is moderated through clear, neutral, and consistently applied rules—not through individual moderators making historical accusations or judgments.
As a Turkish player, I found the treatment of Atatürk in this situation deeply disrespectful. I am not asking for special treatment for Atatürk or for any other historical figure. I am asking for something much simpler: apply the same rules to everyone, do not use personal historical interpretations as moderation judgments, and openly correct mistakes when they occur.
I do not judge a game solely by its gameplay. How a company treats its community is also part of my experience as a paying customer. This incident has seriously damaged my trust in Paradox's community management.

Hearts of Iron IV gibi tarih üzerine kurulu bir oyun geliştiriyorsanız, tarihî kişilikleri ele alırken moderasyonunuzun da aynı ölçüde dikkatli ve tutarlı olmasını beklerim.
Mustafa Kemal Atatürk'ün fotoğrafı üzerinden yaşanan moderasyon süreci ve Atatürk'ün 1915 olaylarıyla ilişkilendirildiği gerekçelendirme benim için kabul edilebilir değildir. Bir moderatörün tarihsel olarak son derece ciddi ve tartışmalı bir konuda kendi yorumunu moderasyon kararının gerekçesine dönüştürmesini doğru bulmuyorum.
Daha da önemlisi, Paradox tarafı daha sonra profil fotoğraflarıyla ilgili kuralın tutarlı biçimde uygulanmadığını kabul etti. Bir topluluk kuralınız varsa bunun kim olduğuna bakılmaksızın aynı ölçütlerle uygulanmasını beklerim. Kuralın bazı tarihî kişilerde uygulanıp bazılarında uygulanmaması, oyuncunun moderasyon sistemine duyduğu güveni zedeler.
Paradox'un sonradan konuyu incelemeye aldığını açıklamasını not ediyorum; ancak benim açımdan mesele yalnızca bir Discord yasağından ibaret değil. Tarih temalı oyunlar üreten uluslararası bir şirketin topluluk yönetiminin, tarihî tartışmalar konusunda kişisel kanaatlerle değil açık, tarafsız ve tutarlı kurallarla hareket etmesi gerekir.
Ben bir Türk oyuncu olarak Atatürk'e yönelik bu yaklaşımı son derece rahatsız edici buldum. Paradox'tan beklediğim herhangi bir tarihî şahsa özel muamele değil; aynı kuralların herkese uygulanması, moderatörlerin tarihsel suç isnatlarını kişisel yorumları üzerinden moderasyon gerekçesine dönüştürmemesi ve yapılan hataların açık biçimde düzeltilmesidir.
Bir oyunu yalnızca oynanışıyla değerlendirmiyorum. Parasını verdiğim şirketin oyuncu topluluğuna nasıl davrandığı da benim kullanıcı deneyimimin bir parçasıdır. Bu olay da Paradox'a ve topluluk yönetimine duyduğum güveni ciddi biçimde sarstı.

I’ve been playing strategy games for years in pretty much every flavor: RTS, grand strategy, real-time combat, economy, diplomacy, you name it. I’ve played Age of Empires II, the Company of Heroes series, Knights of Honor II, and plenty of other strategy games. So I didn’t come into Hearts of Iron IV as someone completely unfamiliar with the genre.

And that’s exactly why my biggest problem with this game is so frustrating:

I feel like I’m spending more time managing the game’s systems than actually making strategic decisions.

I plan a war, and suddenly I’m dealing with division templates, production lines, supply, doctrines, research, organization, fuel, air superiority, frontlines, combat width…

At some point I’m not commanding an army anymore. I’m attending a meeting at the Ministry of War.

In Company of Heroes, putting a unit in the right position and making the right decision gives you immediate feedback. In Knights of Honor II, diplomacy, economy and warfare interact in a way that makes your decisions feel meaningful on the map.

In HOI4, I can make a decision and then spend the next 20 minutes wondering why it worked, why it didn’t work, and which wiki page explains it.

The learning curve is also absurdly steep. I’m all for depth in strategy games. The problem is that HOI4 sometimes crosses the line between “deep” and “needlessly complicated.”

Eventually, instead of thinking about how to win the war, I’m thinking:

“Did I make the correct division template?”

I’m sure the game becomes much more enjoyable once you understand all of its systems. I can absolutely see why people put hundreds or even thousands of hours into it.

But that’s not really the point for me.

I came here to play a strategy game, not to study the instruction manual for a strategy game.

There is an impressive amount of content and detail here, and I won’t deny that. But a lot of that detail feels less like interesting strategic decision-making and more like a collection of variables I constantly have to monitor.

Maybe that’s exactly what some people want.

I just don’t.

I want to manage a war.

I don’t want to manage the accounting department of the war-management simulator.

Mustafa Kemal believed that the army should not become involved in politics while he was a member of İttihat ve Terakki Cemiyeti. At the 1909 congress, he advocated the idea that “the army and the society should be separated.”

In his view, a soldier should not be a politician; a soldier’s duty should be to serve in the army. When the society did not adopt this view, Mustafa Kemal distanced himself from İttihat ve Terakki Cemiyeti and focused on his military duties.

In his speech at the 1909 İttihat ve Terakki Cemiyeti Congress, he stated:

“Let us separate the army from the society. Let the society take root in the nation as a fully-fledged political party, and let the army attend to its primary duty.”

In short, Mustafa Kemal did not want the army to become involved in politics. When he could not reach an agreement with the leadership of İttihat ve Terakki Cemiyeti on this issue, he distanced himself from the organization and devoted himself to his military duties.

As a long-time Turkish player of Hearts of Iron IV, I would like to respectfully share some concerns regarding a recent moderation incident that has attracted considerable attention among Turkish players.

We understand that maintaining a respectful and inclusive community requires clear and consistently applied moderation policies. However, the recent decision to take moderation action against a player for using a photograph of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk as a profile picture, along with the subsequent reference to Atatürk as a “controversial figure,” has raised questions and concerns within the Turkish player community.

Our primary concern is not the moderation of an individual profile, but rather the clarity, consistency, and equal application of the relevant community guidelines. If there are specific rules concerning the use of photographs of historical or public figures as profile pictures, we believe it would be helpful for these rules to be clearly communicated and applied consistently to all members of the community.

We would also like to respectfully raise the issue of Turkish language support in Hearts of Iron IV. Türkiye has a substantial and passionate community of players interested in historical and strategy games. We believe that Turkish localization, as well as stronger communication with Turkish players, could contribute positively to the experience of this community.

Mustafa Kemal Atatürk and the history of the Turkish Republic are subjects of significant historical and cultural importance to Turkish players. For this reason, we hope that related historical content and community matters can be approached with appropriate historical context and sensitivity.

We respectfully ask Paradox Interactive to review the circumstances surrounding this moderation incident, provide clarification regarding the relevant guidelines and moderation decision, and take the concerns raised by Turkish players into consideration.

Our intention is not to create conflict, but to encourage clarity, consistency, and constructive communication.

We value Hearts of Iron IV and the work of the development team. Criticism should not be interpreted as hostility toward the game or its developers. We raise these concerns precisely because we care about the game and would like to see it continue to improve and become more welcoming to players from different communities.

Thank you for taking the time to consider the concerns of the Turkish Hearts of Iron IV community.

Respectfully,
A Turkish Hearts of Iron IV Player

Title: A tedious spreadsheet simulator disguised as a strategy game.Rating: 2/10Do not waste your time or money on this game. What looks like an epic World War II strategy simulator is actually a poorly optimized, frustratingly broken mess that respects neither your time nor your wallet. Brain-Dead Ally AI: The AI is completely incompetent. Your allies will single-handedly lose you the war by flooding your frontlines with hundreds of useless troops, draining all local supplies, and leaving your elite divisions to starve to death in the mud while they do absolutely nothing to help.The Peace Conference Joke: The peace system is an absolute insult to the player. You can suffer millions of casualties, single-handedly capture every enemy capital, and change the course of the war, only for a minor AI country to swoop in during the peace conference and steal half the map, creating horrific, unplayable border-gore. Unplayable Late-Game Lag: The game engine is ancient and cannot handle its own mechanics. By 1943, the game slows down to a mind-numbing crawl because the AI spams thousands of microscopic divisions. It turns into an unplayable slideshow, making it nearly impossible to actually finish a campaign.Greedy DLC Paywall: Paradox’s business model is predatory. The base game is essentially an empty, stripped-down skeleton. Crucial, basic gameplay features—like designing tanks, managing puppet states, or altering ship designs—are intentionally locked behind hundreds of dollars of overpriced DLCs.Incomprehensible Naval Mechanics: The naval system is fundamentally broken. Nobody understands how it works, and the game does a terrible job of explaining it. You can spend hours meticulously building a historical fleet only to have it instantly wiped out by an AI "death-stack" due to hidden, poorly explained modifiers.Logistics Nightmare: The supply system completely kills the fun. The game forces you to micromanage individual railroad tracks and supply hubs rather than focusing on actual grand strategy. Moving your army forward feels like fighting the game's UI rather than fighting an enemy general.Verdict: It is a tedious, expensive, and deeply flawed chore. You will spend 90% of your time angry at broken mechanics, bad AI, and terrible optimization. Avoid at all costs.

If you're going into this game with the enthusiasm of "I'm going to be a World War II commander and conquer the world," gently set that dream on the floor and step away. Hearts of Iron IV is not a strategy game; it is a ruthless Excel spreadsheet with a military camouflage skin. Your first 100 hours will likely be spent just trying to understand what the buttons on the screen actually do.

Here are the harsh realities you will face:

 An Abysmal Tutorial: The in-game tutorial is an absolute joke. It doesn't actually teach you how to play; it just makes you click on a few provinces and then abandons you in a massive, incomprehensible user interface. 

You are practically forced to watch at least 15 to 20 hours of YouTube guides before you even start your first real campaign.
 Excessive Math and Logistics: There is no such thing as "just building tanks and attacking." You have to calculate the "combat width" of your divisions based on specific terrain types, perfectly balance your soft attack and hard attack ratios, and constantly adjust your piercing stats to counter the enemy. Even if you build the strongest army on Earth, if you don't open the logistics map to build railways and supply hubs in the right places, your entire army will starve to death and lose all its equipment without firing a single shot.

 Paradox's DLC Policy: If you only buy the base game, you are essentially just buying a skeleton. Core mechanics that actually make the game enjoyable—like the espionage system, detailed tank and ship designers, or logical national focus trees—are all locked behind DLCs. To get the real HOI4 experience, you either have to drop a massive amount of money on dozens of expansions or get trapped in a monthly subscription model.

 Late-Game Torture: Let's say you figure everything out and successfully make it to 1943 or 1944. The AI will start spamming so many unnecessary, trash-tier divisions onto the frontlines that no matter how powerful your computer's CPU is, the game's engine will choke. Time will slow to a crawl, and the game will turn into a literal slideshow.

 Zero Margin for Error: You can spend hours meticulously micro-managing the perfect front line, only to forget to garrison one random, low-level port in your rear. The AI will launch a tiny naval invasion there, instantly sever your entire supply line, and 10 hours of your hard work will go straight into the garbage in a matter of seconds.

In short, HOI4 is not a casual pastime; it's an unpaid second job. If you aren't ready to sacrifice your mental energy to endless logistics crises and division template statistics, staying far away is the best choice for your sanity.

Paradox Interactive’s latest masterclass in historical illiteracy and corporate cowardice.
Imagine running one of the biggest grand strategy companies on the planet and still somehow employing Discord moderators who think Mustafa Kemal Atatürk is just another “controversial figure” from the HOI4 era, casually tossing him into the same bucket as actual genocidal maniacs because he was once a junior officer in the CUP. Peak brain rot.
A Turkish player puts up a real photo of the founder of the modern Turkish Republic. Instant ban. Reason? “Controversial historical figure.” Follow-up explanation from the genius moderator: Atatürk was in the CUP during 1915 and it’s “controversial” whether he supported or was involved in the events.
Let’s pause and appreciate the pure, uncut historical malpractice here.
In 1915 Mustafa Kemal was commanding the 19th Division at Gallipoli, busy stopping an Allied invasion. He wasn’t sitting in Istanbul drafting deportation orders. He wasn’t in the central government. He wasn’t Enver, Talaat, or Cemal. He was a field officer who later spent years openly criticizing the very CUP leadership that ran the empire into the ground. But sure, let’s just smear the entire man with the broadest, laziest brush possible because reading more than a Wikipedia summary is apparently optional at Paradox.
Then they had the absolute gall to compare him to Karl Marx as another “polarizing modern political figure.” Marx never founded a republic, never modernized a collapsed empire, never fought at Gallipoli, and never became the literal Father of the Nation for tens of millions of people. But sure, same category. Why not?
The double standard is so cartoonish it’s almost impressive. Stalin portraits? Apparently fine in some corners. Other far more toxic historical figures? Whatever. But the guy who pulled Turkey out of the wreckage of the Ottoman Empire and built a secular republic? Too spicy for Discord. Can’t have that.
And of course when the Turkish playerbase (one of the largest and most dedicated for Paradox games) rightfully lost their minds and review-bombed the living hell out of HOI4 until the recent reviews hit “Overwhelmingly Negative,” Paradox’s response was the classic corporate non-apology: “We’ll review the rule… it wasn’t enforced consistently.” No full ownership. No firing of the historically illiterate moderator. No clear statement that linking Atatürk to 1915 in that way was a grotesque overreach. Just the usual “lessons will be learned” corporate sludge while the damage is already done.
This is what happens when a company that makes games about history hires people who treat history like a TikTok comment section. Zero nuance, maximum ideology, and zero respect for the fact that different nations actually revere their founding figures for reasons that aren’t up for random moderator reinterpretation.
Paradox didn’t just ban a profile picture. They publicly insulted the national founder of a major playerbase with a half-baked, context-free historical smear, then acted surprised when the backlash hit like a freight train. Absolute clown show from top to bottom.

As a Turkish player, I find it absolutely unacceptable that someone was reportedly banned from the official Hearts of Iron IV Discord server simply for using a photograph of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the founder of the Republic of Türkiye, as their profile picture.

How can a company that develops historical strategy games allow its community moderators to treat one of the most significant figures in modern Turkish history this way?

Atatürk is not just a historical figure to millions of people. He is the founder of our republic and a symbol of independence, sovereignty, and modernization. Disrespecting his legacy and spreading questionable historical claims about him is deeply offensive to the Turkish gaming community.

I expect Paradox Interactive to investigate this incident, provide a transparent explanation, and hold its moderation team accountable for its decisions.

Until this matter is properly addressed, I cannot recommend this game.

Disappointed by Paradox’s moderation and the apparent double standards.
Recent moderation decisions regarding players using Atatürk as a profile picture are deeply concerning. The moderator explicitly justified the action by referring to Atatürk’s alleged “support or involvement” in the Armenian events of 1915, while similar historical and political figures appear to be treated differently. If the rule is that controversial political figures cannot be used as profile pictures, it should be applied consistently to everyone, regardless of nationality or historical controversy.

Even more concerning are reports of Turkish members’ comments being removed when they challenge or criticize this decision. Suppressing criticism instead of addressing it openly creates the impression that legitimate disagreement is being silenced rather than moderated fairly. This seems difficult to reconcile with principles of equal treatment, open discussion, and consistent moderation.

There is also a historical problem with the moderator’s justification. Atatürk had a past connection to the Committee of Union and Progress, but that alone does not make him a decision-maker or establish personal responsibility for the Armenian events of 1915. Presenting his alleged involvement as a moderation justification without providing proper historical context is an oversimplification of a highly complex historical subject.

Paradox has every right to establish rules for its communities, but those rules should be clear, consistently applied, historically responsible, and equally enforced. What makes this situation particularly disappointing is not simply the decision itself, but the apparent inconsistency and the handling of people who object to it.

Buradaki mesele yalnızca bir Discord banı değildir. Asıl mesele, Türkiye Cumhuriyeti’nin kurucusu ve Türk tarihinin en önemli isimlerinden biri olan Mustafa Kemal Atatürk’ün, bir oyuncunun profil fotoğrafında yer almasının moderasyon tarafından siyasi veya tartışmalı bir unsur olarak değerlendirilmesi ve bunun sonucunda oyuncuya yaptırım uygulanmasıdır.

Bir şirketin kendi topluluk kurallarını belirleme hakkına elbette saygı duyuyorum. Ancak bu kuralların kimlere, hangi gerekçelerle ve ne şekilde uygulandığı da aynı ölçüde önemlidir. Özellikle farklı tarihî ve siyasi figürlere yönelik uygulamaların tutarlılığı konusunda ortaya çıkan soru işaretleri, benim Paradox’un topluluk yönetimine olan güvenimi ciddi şekilde zedelemiştir.

Paradox’un bu olayla ilgili yalnızca kuralı değiştirmekle kalmayıp, yaşanan moderasyon sürecini açık biçimde ele alması ve Türk oyuncu topluluğunun neden tepki gösterdiğini gerçekten anlaması gerektiğini düşünüyorum.

**Hearts of Iron IV (HoI4)** has slowly started to feel less like a grand strategy game and more like a giant pile of mechanics that you have to keep track of. At times, it genuinely feels like you're managing an Excel spreadsheet with a World War II skin on it. The game has received years of updates and DLC, but a lot of the problems that have been around for a long time are still there. Meanwhile, Paradox keeps adding more systems and paid expansions under the idea of "continuous development."

The AI is probably the biggest example of this. After all these years, it still struggles with some pretty basic things, especially supply and logistics. You can see AI countries putting huge numbers of divisions into areas that clearly don't have enough supply, leaving parts of a frontline almost completely empty, or sending naval invasions that they have no real way of supporting. Sometimes you don't feel like you outplayed the enemy. You just watched the AI do something obviously stupid and took advantage of it.

The DLC situation is another thing that gets frustrating. I'm not against DLC or expanding the game. HoI4 has obviously benefited from having more content. The problem is that some of the older systems still feel awkward while new mechanics keep getting added on top of them. Peace conferences are still a good example of this, and frontline management can be incredibly annoying when the game decides to do something you didn't want it to do. Some newer focus trees are also so heavily scripted that they can feel less like giving you options and more like following a giant list of predetermined paths. Alternate history is one of HoI4's biggest strengths, so it's a bit strange when certain countries end up feeling more restricted because of how their focus trees are designed.

The UI doesn't really make things easier either. There are so many icons, modifiers, notifications, menus and tooltips that it can be difficult to tell what actually matters. This is obviously worse for new players, but even after playing for a long time, there are moments where you have to stop and figure out what some random modifier or notification is actually trying to tell you.

And then there's the late-game performance. The longer a campaign goes on, the more the game has to keep track of: more divisions, more battles, more countries, more equipment, more calculations and so on. Eventually the game can slow down quite a lot, even on relatively powerful PCs. It's especially annoying because the 1940s should be when the war is getting more interesting, not when you're sitting there waiting for each day to tick over.

That said, I don't think HoI4 is a bad game. Far from it. The amount of content, the alternate-history possibilities and especially the modding community are a huge part of why people have played it for so long. You can have completely different campaigns depending on what country you choose and what decisions you make, and that's something a lot of other strategy games simply don't offer in the same way.

That's also why the problems are so frustrating. There's a genuinely great game underneath all of this, but after years of adding new mechanics, the game has become harder to manage without necessarily becoming better in the areas that matter most. Sometime

A war simulator where the only thing you'll lose is your will to live

Hearts of Iron IV is a game where you spend 90% of your time staring at a map and 10% wondering why your 40 divisions are standing in a field instead of fighting.

The AI is a war crime against intelligence. Germany will sit there with 300 divisions and never attack anyone. Italy will invade Ethiopia, lose, and somehow still be a "major power". The Soviets will trade half their army for a mountain you never asked about. And yes, France will still fold in six weeks, no matter how you set it up.

The combat system is a black box. Width, stacking, supply, organization, reinforcement, terrain, and the mystery modifier you didn't know about all combine to tell you that your 100 divisions lost to 12. Why? The game won't say.

The division designer is homework. You need a spreadsheet, three wiki tabs, and a degree in logistics just to build an infantry template that doesn't fall apart.

The late game is a slideshow. By 1943, your PC sounds like a jet engine and the game runs like a flipbook. Speed 5 is a lie.

Verdict: It's a game that rewards you for reading a guide, punishes you for having fun, and asks you to pay hundreds of dollars for the privilege. 1/10. The point is for the music, because at least it sounds like you're winning.

**Son derece hayal kırıklığı yaratan bir oyun ve oyuncuyu sürekli DLC almaya zorlayan bir sistem.**

Hearts of Iron IV, sahip olduğu potansiyele rağmen yıllar içerisinde oyuncuya giderek daha fazla içerik satmaya odaklanan bir ürüne dönüştü. Temel oyunun üzerine sürekli yeni DLC'ler eklenmesi artık bir geliştirme modelinden çok, parçalanmış içeriğin tekrar tekrar ücretlendirilmesi hissini veriyor.

En büyük sorunlardan biri, oyunun fiyatının tek başına değerlendirilmesinin mümkün olmaması. Oyunun gerçekten kapsamlı bir deneyim haline gelmesi için çok sayıda DLC satın almak gerekiyor. Üstelik bu DLC'lerin toplam maliyeti, bir oyuncunun makul bir şekilde bekleyebileceği seviyeleri çoktan aşmış durumda.

Bunun karşılığında ise teknik problemler, performans sorunları, yapay zekânın zaman zaman anlamsız davranışları ve yıllardır tamamen çözülemeyen mekanik problemlerle karşılaşabiliyorsunuz. Oyuncuların geri bildirimleri yıllardır ortadayken bazı problemlerin sürekli yeniden karşımıza çıkması ciddi şekilde rahatsız edici.

**Paradox'un DLC politikası özellikle eleştirilmeyi hak ediyor.** Bir oyunu uzun yıllar desteklemek elbette değerli bir şeydir; ancak uzun süre desteklemek ile oyunu sürekli parçalara bölüp her parçayı ayrı ayrı satmak aynı şey değildir.

Hearts of Iron IV'ün temel fikri ve potansiyeli gerçekten çok iyi. Fakat bu potansiyelin önüne geçen şey artık oyunun kendisinden çok, etrafında oluşturulan ticari model.

Bir strateji oyununa yüzlerce saat ayırmak isteyen oyuncudan sürekli yeni DLC satın almasını beklemek yerine, önce mevcut oyunun temel problemlerinin çözülmesini ve oyuncuya gerçekten tamamlanmış bir ürün sunulmasını beklerdim.

**Kısacası: Harika bir fikrin üzerine kurulmuş, fakat zamanla oyuncuyu memnun etmekten çok oyuncudan mümkün olduğunca fazla gelir elde etmeye odaklanmış gibi görünen bir sistem.**

Bu haliyle tavsiye etmiyorum.
**A deeply disappointing experience and one of the clearest examples of an excessive DLC-driven business model.**

Hearts of Iron IV has enormous potential, but after years of development, the game increasingly feels like a product designed around selling additional DLC rather than delivering a complete and polished strategy experience.

The biggest problem is that the base game can no longer reasonably be evaluated on its own. If you want a genuinely comprehensive experience, you are expected to purchase a large number of DLCs. The combined cost has reached a point that is difficult to justify for what is, fundamentally, a single strategy game.

And what do you get in return? Performance problems, technical issues, questionable AI behavior, unbalanced mechanics, and long-standing problems that continue to resurface years after release.

Long-term support is not inherently a bad thing. In fact, it can be one of the best aspects of a strategy game. But there is a huge difference between supporting a game for years and repeatedly dividing the experience into separate paid pieces.

**Paradox's DLC strategy deserves serious criticism.** At some point, continuous monetization stops feeling like additional support and starts feeling like the player is being charged repeatedly for an experience that should have been more complete in the first place.

The frustrating part is that Hearts of Iron IV itself could have been an exceptional game. The concept is brilliant, the strategic possibilities are enormous, and the modding community has demonstrated just how much potential this game has.

But the commercial model surrounding the game increasingly overshadows the game itself.

Players should not have to keep opening their wallets simply to make an already expensive game feel complete.

**In short: an excellent concept buried under an exhausting DLC strategy, persistent technical problems, and a business model that increasingly feels more focused on monetization than on delivering a complete player experience.**

I cannot recommend it in its current state.

I am leaving a negative review because of the recent conduct and statements surrounding the Hearts of Iron community.

I have no problem with criticism, historical debate, or different opinions. However, when a company or its community representatives use racist, populist, or exclusionary rhetoric, especially when it appears to single out a particular group of players, I cannot simply ignore it.

As a Turkish player, seeing Atatürk and Turkish players become the subject of this kind of controversy is deeply disappointing. Historical figures can and should be discussed critically, but there is a clear difference between legitimate historical discussion and rhetoric that alienates or belittles an entire group of players.

I have enjoyed Paradox games for years, but a good game does not excuse a company or its community spaces from treating their players with basic respect.

For that reason, I am leaving a negative review. This is not a review of the game's mechanics or quality. It is a statement about the attitude and communication surrounding the game and the community.

I hope Paradox understands that Turkish players are also a significant part of its community, and that respect should apply equally to everyone.

I’ve supported Paradox games because they are supposed to be about history, politics, nations, and complex historical perspectives. But there is a huge difference between discussing history critically and allowing moderators to casually reduce the founder of modern Türkiye, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, to labels such as “racist” and “genocider.”

Atatürk is not some fictional character for moderators to throw inflammatory labels at for entertainment. He is one of the most important political and military figures of the 20th century and the founder of the Republic of Türkiye. His legacy can absolutely be debated — like the legacy of virtually every major historical leader — but serious historical discussion requires evidence, context, and consistent standards.

If Paradox wants its communities to discuss controversial historical figures, then moderate those discussions professionally. If moderators are allowed to make sweeping accusations themselves, don't pretend the community is being held to some sophisticated standard of historical discussion.

And here is the bigger problem: Paradox sells games built around real countries, cultures, wars, religions and historical leaders. Turkish players are customers too. You cannot happily sell us content based on our history and then expect us to shrug when people representing your community moderation use inflammatory accusations about the founder of our republic.

Criticize Atatürk's policies. Debate his decisions. Discuss difficult periods of Ottoman and Turkish history. Bring sources. That's history.

Reducing an enormously complicated historical figure to “racist” and “genocider” without serious context isn't historical analysis. It's inflammatory moderation dressed up as history.

Paradox should ask itself a very simple question: would it consider this standard of language acceptable from its moderators when discussing every country's most significant historical figures?

If the answer is no, Turkish history should not be treated as the exception.

Do better, Paradox. Your Turkish players deserve the same professionalism and respect you expect from the communities you're moderating.

I have been playing Hearts of Iron IV for a long time and I genuinely appreciate the depth, historical setting, and amount of content that Paradox has created. However, I was very disappointed by the way Atatürk is portrayed and mocked in the game.

Historical games do not have to portray every historical figure positively. Criticism, alternative interpretations, and controversial historical events are all perfectly reasonable parts of a grand strategy game. However, there is a difference between presenting history in a critical or fictionalized way and simply making a historical figure the subject of ridicule.

Mustafa Kemal Atatürk is not just an ordinary historical character for Turkish players. He played a central role in the Turkish War of Independence and in the establishment and modernization of the Republic of Türkiye. Whatever someone's personal opinion of his political legacy may be, his historical importance is undeniable. Because of this, treating him as a joke can understandably come across as disrespectful to many Turkish players.

What disappoints me most is that Hearts of Iron IV is a game that otherwise puts a great deal of effort into historical detail. When a game presents itself around real historical events, leaders, countries, and ideologies, I think it should also show some consistency in how it handles historically significant figures. Humor and alternate history can certainly have a place in the game, but there are ways to do that without unnecessarily mocking figures who have enormous historical and cultural significance to millions of people.

I am not asking Paradox to remove historical criticism or to portray Atatürk as a perfect person. That would not be appropriate for a historical strategy game either. My point is simply that historical representation should be handled with some degree of context and respect, especially when dealing with figures whose legacy remains extremely important to an entire nation.

As a Turkish player, seeing Atatürk treated this way significantly reduced my enjoyment of this aspect of the game. I hope Paradox will reconsider how such historical figures are represented in future updates and content. Hearts of Iron IV is capable of much better historical storytelling, and I would much rather see the game use that potential than rely on cheap jokes at the expense of historically important figures.

Mesele yalnızca Atatürk değil. Asıl soru şu: Bir kullanıcının seçtiği tarihsel figürle hangi topluluk kuralını ihlal ettiği nasıl birbirinden ayrılıyor?

Kullanıcı hakaret ettiyse, tehditte bulunduysa veya kuralları açıkça çiğnediyse, bunun somut biçimde gösterilmesi gerekir. Ancak ortada yalnızca bir profil fotoğrafı ve tartışmalı bir tarihsel konu varsa, bunu doğrudan ban gerekçesine dönüştürmek ciddi bir tutarsızlıktır.

Üstelik bu, alternatif tarih senaryoları üzerine kurulu bir oyunun topluluğunda yaşanıyor. Oyunda tarihin akışını değiştirmek serbest; Discord’da ise hangi tarihsel kimliğin temsil edilebileceği moderasyonun takdirine bırakılıyor.

Yani oyunda ülke sınırlarını değiştirebiliyor, rejimleri devirebiliyor, tarihin akışını baştan yazabiliyorsunuz. Ama Discord’da bir profil fotoğrafı seçerken moderasyon ekibinin tarih anlayışına uygun davranmanız gerekiyor. Alternatif tarih serbest, alternatif profil fotoğrafı riskli.

Türkiye’de oyuncuların desteğini isteyen bir şirket, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk’le ilgili profil fotoğrafları ve tarihsel görüşler konusunda açık, tutarlı ve herkese eşit uygulanan kurallar belirlemeli. Aksi halde ortaya şu çelişki çıkıyor:

Tarihi simüle etmek serbest, fakat bazı tarihsel kimlikleri taşımak sakıncalı.

He led the Turkish War of Independence against the occupation of Anatolia following the First World War and played a decisive role in the establishment of the Grand National Assembly and an independent Turkish state. Beyond his military achievements, Atatürk led the political, legal, educational, and social transformation of the newly established Republic of Türkiye. The proclamation of the Republic, the transition toward a secular legal system, educational reforms, the adoption of the modern Turkish alphabet, and the expansion of women's political rights were among the major changes carried out under his leadership. The historical context and consequences of these reforms can be studied and discussed academically; however, Atatürk's central role in the founding of modern Türkiye and the national independence struggle is grounded in concrete historical facts. Hearts of Iron IV çok iyi bir grand strategy oyunu olabilir ama bazı mekanikleri artık gerçekten oyuncunun sabrını test ediyor.

Özellikle **supply sistemi**, gerçekçilik adına tasarlanmış olmasına rağmen bazı durumlarda stratejik karar vermekten çok “neden birliklerim burada savaşmıyor?” diye lojistik ekranını kontrol ettiğin bir angaryaya dönüşüyor. Because of this disrespectful and biased treatment, we are boycotting the game and any future DLCs. Bir tarih oyunu geliştiricisinin kendi tarih bilgisini ve topluluk yönetimini sorgulatacak noktaya gelmesi gerçekten inanılmaz.

Paradox Interactive’in resmî Hearts of Iron IV Discord sunucusunda bir Türk oyuncudan, profil fotoğrafındaki Mustafa Kemal Atatürk’ün gerçek portresini kaldırmasının istenmesi ve bunun “tartışmalı/kutuplaştırıcı bir tarihî figür” olduğu gerekçesiyle savunulması kabul edilebilir değil.

Daha da vahimi, bu karar savunulurken Atatürk’ü 1915 olaylarıyla ilişkilendiren tartışmalı tarihsel iddiaların moderasyon gerekçesi hâline getirilmesi. Tarih üzerine oyunlar üretip milyonlarca oyuncuya tarihsel senaryolar satan bir şirketin resmî topluluğunda böyle ciddi bir konuda bu kadar özensiz, taraflı ve sorumsuz bir yaklaşım görmek tam anlamıyla hayal kırıklığı.

Ancak sorun sadece tek bir moderatörün söylediği sözlerden ibaret değil.

Oyuncular kararı sorgulamaya başladığında eleştirileri susturmak, mesajları kaldırmak ve tepki gösteren kullanıcıları uzaklaştırmak çözüm değildir. Topluluk yönetimi, şirketinizi eleştiren insanları susturmak değil; uyguladığınız kararların arkasında şeffaf, tutarlı ve savunulabilir gerekçeler sunabilmektir.

Atatürk, Türkiye Cumhuriyeti'nin kurucusudur ve milyonlarca insan için sıradan bir “politik sembol” değildir. Gerçek fotoğrafının sorun sayılıp aynı kişinin HOI4 içerisindeki çiziminin kullanılmasına izin verilmesi ise alınan kararın ne kadar absürt bir noktaya geldiğini ayrıca gösteriyor.

Yıllardır oyuncularınızdan ana oyunlar, genişleme paketleri ve sayısız DLC için para alıyorsunuz. Buna karşılık oyuncuların beklediği en temel şeylerden biri de topluluklarına ve tarihsel hassasiyetlerine saygılı davranılmasıdır.

Eleştiriye sansürle, tarihsel tartışmalara keyfî moderasyonla cevap veren bir topluluk yönetimini desteklemiyorum.

Paradox yönetiminden beklenen şey çok basit:

Yaşananları açıkça araştırın, moderasyon kararının nasıl ve neden alındığını açıklayın, hatalı uygulamalar varsa sorumluluk alın ve en büyük oyuncu topluluklarınızdan biri olan Türk oyuncu topluluğuna karşı aynı durumun tekrar yaşanmayacağını garanti edecek açık kurallar oluşturun.

Sessizlik de bir cevaptır.

Ve şu ana kadar verilen cevap kesinlikle yeterli değil.

Bu mesele çözülene ve Paradox açık, ciddi ve tatmin edici bir açıklama yapana kadar şirketin oyunlarını veya DLC'lerini tavsiye etmiyorum.

Hearts of Iron IV promises to put the Second World War in your hands. What it actually delivers is a spreadsheet with a tank skin, bolted to an AI that seems to have learned warfare from watching someone else lose at it.
The core problem is the frontline system. You draw an arrow, press a button, and hope. When it works, it feels automated to the point of irrelevance. When it fails, and it often does, your divisions shuffle back and forth between provinces like confused tourists while the enemy walks through the gap you were supposedly defending. Micromanaging by hand fixes this, but then the game becomes a clicking marathon, and the "grand" in grand strategy quietly disappears.
The AI deserves its own paragraph. It launches naval invasions into your capital with three divisions and no supply, yet somehow cannot hold a river line with forty. Historical nations make decisions no historical government would make, and playing against it for more than a few campaigns exposes how little it understands its own mechanics.

Hearts of Iron IV (HOI4), tarihsel gerçeklikler ve askeri liderler üzerine kurulu bir strateji oyunu olmasına rağmen, resmi Discord sunucusunda son dönemde yaşananlar kabul edilemez bir çifte standardı ve açık bir ayrımcılığı gözler önüne sermektedir. Türkiye Cumhuriyeti'nin kurucusu Mustafa Kemal Atatürk ve Türk tarihine mal olmuş bağımsızlık mücadelesi veren Türk Paşalarının profil fotoğraflarını kullanan Türk kullanıcılar, asılsız ve mesnetsiz gerekçelerle sunucudan uzaklaştırılmıştır.

1. Kabul Edilemez Çifte Standart ve Tarihsel İkiyüzlülük
HOI4, doğası gereği 20. yüzyılın en kanlı diktatörlerini, ideolojik liderlerini ve askeri figürlerini oyun içi birer öğe olarak sunmaktadır. Paradox Interactive, oyuncu topluluğuna karşı adil, eşitlikçi ve saygılı olmak zorundadır. On Community Rights and Biased Moderation: Paradox Interactive’s Discriminatory Stance Against Turkish Players
Although Hearts of Iron IV (HOI4) is a grand strategy game built around historical realities and military figures, recent events on its official Discord server have exposed an unacceptable double standard and blatant discrimination. Turkish users carrying profile pictures of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk—the founder of the Republic of Türkiye—and other prominent Turkish commanders and pashas have been banned from the server under groundless and absurd pretexts.

This approach goes beyond an isolated moderation mistake; it directly brings into question the existence of a systemic bias and discriminatory stance toward Turkish identity and history within Paradox Interactive's community management.

Savaşın sonunda, Osmanlı İmparatorluğu'nun yenilgisini izleyen Kurtuluş Savaşı ile simgelenen Anadolu Hareketi'ne öncülük ve önderlik etti. Türk Kurtuluş Savaşı sürecinde Ankara Hükûmeti'ni kurdu, Türk Orduları Başkomutanı olarak Sakarya Meydan Muharebesi'ndeki başarısından dolayı 19 Eylül 1921 tarihinde "gazi" sanını aldı ve mareşallik rütbesine yükseldi. I really wanted to love this game, but after sinking a lot of hours into it, I just can't recommend it in its current state.

First off, the AI is completely brain-dead. In single-player, the computer will happily grind millions of its own men into your entrenched positions for zero strategic gain, or it will suddenly pull all its units off a front line to redeploy them across the continent, leaving you to just walk into their capital. It completely ruins the immersion and eliminates any real challenge once you understand the basic mechanics.

Then there’s the pricing model. The base game feels like an empty demo. Paradox has stripped out basic quality-of-life features and locked them behind an endless paywall of DLCs. You basically need to spend a small fortune just to design equipment properly, manage puppets, or have functional naval and air mechanics.

On top of that, the late-game performance is brutal. Once 1942–1943 hits, the game engine chokes under the weight of thousands of useless minor-nation divisions, and the game slows down to an unbearable crawl even on a solid PC.

The game also suffers from bloated micromanagement. Instead of focusing on macro grand strategy, you spend half your time in tedious designer menus tweaking tank engines and plane modules just to follow an arbitrary meta, only for the war to end in an absolute mess of border gore during the peace conference.

If it weren't for the passionate modding community, this game would be nearly unplayable. Grab it on a heavy sale if you really like WW2 strategy, but be prepared to buy expensive DLCs and download overhaul mods just to get a competent experience.

Hearts of Iron IV has stopped being an enjoyable strategy game for me and has become unnecessarily complicated and exhausting.

Over time, the game has been filled with so many details and systems that I feel like I spend more time dealing with menus and mechanics than actually making strategic decisions. The learning curve is already extremely steep for new players, and even for longtime players, the constant addition of new mechanics eventually takes away from the fun.

The DLC policy has also become incredibly frustrating. New content is constantly being added on top of the base game, and having so much of it locked behind paid DLC makes the game feel less like a complete experience and more like something that constantly asks you to spend more money.

What I used to love about HOI4 was its grand strategy. Now, it feels buried under an excessive amount of details, systems, and content. Making everything more detailed does not automatically make a game better.

As someone who has played the game for a long time, I can honestly say that it now feels more like a chore than entertainment. Instead of adding more DLC and more mechanics, I think the developers should focus on simplifying the experience, improving accessibility, and making the actual gameplay fun again.

I really wanted to enjoy Hearts of Iron IV, but for me it ended up feeling more exhausting than fun.

The game has a lot of systems, but too often complexity replaces actual depth. You spend an incredible amount of time dealing with menus, micromanagement, production, focus trees, broken AI behavior and systems that feel unnecessarily complicated.

The AI is still one of my biggest problems with the game. Frontlines can behave terribly, allies make completely irrational decisions, and late-game wars can become both frustrating and painfully slow.

After a while, I stopped feeling like I was playing a grand strategy game and started feeling like I was just managing endless menus.

The amount of DLC also makes the whole experience worse for me. Instead of fixing some of the fundamental problems, it often feels like even more systems and content are added on top.

I was also personally uncomfortable with discussions and allegations I came across regarding racist remarks connected to people around the development side. I think everyone should research that topic themselves and make their own judgment, but it definitely affected how I felt about supporting the game.

My biggest problem with HOI4 isn't that it's difficult.

It's that after spending so many hours on it, I often felt like I had simply wasted my time.

It is genuinely disappointing to see a company that builds games around history display such a careless and superficial understanding of history when it actually matters.

A Turkish player was banned from your official Discord server for using a photograph of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk as their profile picture, with the justification that Atatürk is a “controversial” or “polarizing” historical figure. That would already be questionable enough. What makes this situation even worse is the attempt to justify the decision by directly associating Atatürk with the events of 1915 and the Committee of Union and Progress.

Mustafa Kemal was not the head of the Ottoman government in 1915. He was not a member of the wartime cabinet. He was not the person directing the Ottoman government’s policies regarding the events of 1915. He was an Ottoman military officer serving at Gallipoli.

If you are going to make historical strategy games, the least people should expect is a serious understanding of the historical figures and events you are talking about, rather than connecting them through a few superficial associations.

And this is not merely a disagreement over historical interpretation. Banning someone for using a photograph of Atatürk, suppressing people who challenge the decision, and then presenting this as “neutral moderation” is an extremely poor way to manage a community.

Whether someone likes Atatürk or dislikes him is a separate matter. You do not have to be Turkish to recognize his historical significance. Mustafa Kemal Atatürk is one of the most important military and political figures of the 20th century. Reducing him to just another “controversial profile picture” is an incredibly superficial approach, especially for the community surrounding a historical strategy game.

There is something deeply ironic about a company making games about history while demonstrating such a shallow understanding of historical context within its own community.

You make historical strategy games. Start by learning the history.

This is the founder and first President of the Republic of Türkiye. A leader whose legacy in Türkiye includes dedicating 23 April to children and 19 May to youth; a leader who placed extraordinary importance on younger generations and entrusted the future of the Republic to them.
We grow up learning his reforms, his principles and his Address to the Youth. These are not meaningless details to millions of Turkish people. They are part of the history and civic culture of our country.
Historical figures can of course be discussed and debated. Nobody is asking Paradox or its moderators to adopt a particular political interpretation of history.
But there is a major difference between allowing historical discussion and deciding that the mere photograph of the founder of a country is itself unacceptable because he has been labelled “controversial.”
As a Turkish customer, I find that moderation decision discriminatory and deeply disrespectful.
If your rule is genuinely about preventing political arguments, then apply that rule consistently to political arguments. Do not turn the photograph of a country's founding president into prohibited content simply because someone has decided that the person is “controversial.”
I enjoyed these games. I supported this company. I wanted to buy more of its games.

Labeling Mustafa Kemal Atatürk with politically charged terms like "genocidal" within these Discord servers stems not from rigorous historiography, but from digital orientalism and toxic edgelord subculture. Reducing a anti-imperialist war of independence fought against foreign occupation—alongside a comprehensive secular modernization movement—to baseless accusations of genocide is a blatant exercise in historical revisionism. The moderation tactics observed on these platforms constitute a form of veiled hate speech disguised as community guidelines. It is profoundly hypocritical that servers granting boundless leeway to far-right, monarchist, or totalitarian discourse under the pretext of "alternate history humor" suddenly adopt aggressive censorship when confronted with the founding figure of the Turkish Republic. The problem isn't that DLC exists. Expansions are perfectly reasonable. The problem is that core parts of a game are repeatedly cut out and sold separately, while more and more DLC keeps piling on top of the old content.

I want to buy a game because it's good; I don't want to calculate which 15 DLCs I need just to make the game feel complete.

Paradox, stop treating your most loyal players like an endless source of DLC revenue. Make complete games, release meaningful expansions, and show some respect for the players who have supported you for years.

Bu olayın en rahatsız edici yanı yalnızca bir profil fotoğrafının yasaklanması değil; bu kararın gerekçelendirilmesinde sergilenen tarihsel özensizliktir.

Mustafa Kemal Atatürk gibi 20. yüzyılın askerî ve siyasî tarihine belirgin biçimde etki etmiş bir şahsiyeti “controversial” etiketiyle geçiştirmek zaten son derece yüzeysel bir yaklaşım. Ancak çok daha ciddi olanı, onun İttihat ve Terakki ile tarihsel ilişkisini alıp buradan 1915 olaylarına ilişkin “support or involvement” imasında bulunmaktır.

Tarih böyle yazılmaz.

Mustafa Kemal’in gençlik döneminde İttihat ve Terakki ile ilişkisi tarih yazımında bilinen ve incelenen bir konudur. Fakat bir örgütle belirli bir dönemde ilişki veya üyelik, o örgütün daha sonraki bütün kararlarından otomatik olarak bireysel sorumluluk doğurmaz. Böyle bir sorumluluk iddia ediyorsanız; karar mekanizmasını, emir-komuta zincirini, kişinin fiilî görevini, yazışmalarını, eylemlerini ve dönemin birincil kaynaklarını ortaya koymanız gerekir.

1915’te Mustafa Kemal’in fiilî görevi Çanakkale Cephesi’ndeydi. İttihat ve Terakki’nin savaş yıllarındaki merkezî siyasî kadrosuyla Mustafa Kemal’in konumu arasındaki fark da ciddi tarih literatüründe tartışılmış bir meseledir. Dolayısıyla birkaç kelimelik bir moderasyon mesajında, örgütsel bağlantıdan hareket ederek “support or involvement” gibi son derece ağır bir imada bulunmak tarihçilik değil, tarihsel bağlamı ortadan kaldırmaktır.

Ayrıca kendi görüşümü de açıkça ifade edeyim: Ben 1915 olaylarının “soykırım” olarak nitelendirilmesine katılmıyorum. Bunun, siyasî veya kurumsal bir etiketin tartışmasız biçimde tekrarlanmasıyla kapatılabilecek bir mesele olduğunu da düşünmüyorum. Osmanlı, Ermeni ve üçüncü ülke arşivlerinin karşılaştırılması; demografik verilerin, emirlerin, uygulamaların, savaş koşullarının ve karşılıklı şiddet vakalarının birlikte incelenmesi; farklı görüşlerdeki tarihçilerin aynı akademik zeminde tartışabilmesi gerektiğini düşünüyorum.

Elbette 1915’in niteliğine ilişkin uluslararası akademik ve hukuki tartışmalarda benim görüşümden farklı çok sayıda değerlendirme bulunmaktadır. Benim itirazım bunların varlığına değil; böylesine ağır ve karmaşık bir tarihsel meselenin tartışılmaz bir ön kabul haline getirilmesine ve daha sonra bu ön kabulden hareketle Mustafa Kemal gibi kişilere delilsiz biçimde kişisel sorumluluk ima edilmesine yöneliktir.

Bir tarihsel nitelendirmeyi kabul etmek başka şeydir; belirli bir kişiye bireysel sorumluluk atfetmek başka şeydir. İkincisi için ayrıca ve doğrudan kanıt gerekir.

Aynı şekilde “controversial historical figure” ifadesi, açık ve tutarlı kriterleri olmadığı sürece tarihsel bir kategori değil, keyfî bir moderasyon etiketidir. Dünya tarihinde etkili olmuş neredeyse her devlet adamı, asker, düşünür veya devrimci birileri açısından “controversial”dır. Eğer bu kavram bir profil fotoğrafını yasaklamak için kullanılacaksa, kriterlerinin evrensel, açık ve bütün tarihî şahsiyetlere eşit biçimde uygulanması gerekir.

Özellikle tarih üzerine oyunlar üreten bir şirketten beklenen şey, tarihi sloganlara ve birkaç cümlelik çağdaş politik kategorilere indirgemek değil; kaynak, kronoloji ve bağlam konusunda ortalama bir internet tartışmasından daha yüksek bir standart göstermektir.

Dear Paradox Interactive Support and Community Management,
I am writing to you as a dedicated member of the Paradox gaming community. Turkey represents one of the largest and most passionate player bases for your strategy games, especially Hearts of Iron IV. However, I am submitting this formal complaint regarding unacceptable moderation practices and defamatory actions on the official HoI4 Discord server carried out by moderator @chakerathe (Discord ID: 186828692054343680 / <@86828692054343680>).

This moderator has been actively banning Turkish users for using the real-life portrait of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the founder of the Republic of Turkey, while falsely attempting to link him to the 1915 events to justify these bans.

These claims are entirely false, historically illiterate, and defamatory. The historical facts are clear and indisputable:
1. Zero Involvement: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk had absolutely no connection, role, or responsibility in the 1915 events.
2. Severed Political Ties: Atatürk completely severed all ties with the Committee of Union and Progress (CUP) as early as their 1909 congress.
3. Historical Reality: In 1915, Atatürk was serving as an army officer at the Gallipoli Front—hundreds of kilometers away from Eastern Anatolia—strictly defending the homeland.

Falsely associating a respected nation's founding leader with baseless allegations is an act of defamation and an insult to the Turkish community. Furthermore, enforcing a ban on Atatürk's portrait under the pretext of "controversial real-life figures" while routinely permitting real-life profile pictures of political leaders associated with documented mass atrocities (such as Stalin or Churchill) exposes a blatant double standard.

We demand the following immediate actions:
1. Immediate Removal of Profile Restrictions: Unconditional lifting of the ban on real-life images of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk across the official Discord server.
2. Investigation into Moderator Misconduct: A formal review regarding moderator <@86828692054343680> (@chakerathe) for abusing authority, spreading false historical claims, and target-banning Turkish users.
3. Reinstatement of Accounts: The unconditional unbanning of all users who were unjustly penalized under these false pretexts.

We expect Paradox Interactive to uphold historical integrity and ensure its official community channels remain free from personal political biases against its player base.
Sincerely,

I have enjoyed Hearts of Iron IV for a long time, but the way the recent Mustafa Kemal Atatürk controversy was handled by the official community has completely changed my view of how this game is being represented.

On the official Hearts of Iron IV Discord server, a Turkish player was reportedly removed for using a photograph of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk as their profile picture. The justification was that Atatürk is considered a “controversial and divisive political figure.”

That alone would already be questionable. What makes the situation significantly worse are the statements made by moderation regarding Atatürk's historical role, including attempts to associate him with the events of 1915 and the Committee of Union and Progress.

These are highly sensitive and historically disputed subjects. Presenting such claims in the context of moderating a user's profile — rather than treating them as matters of historical discussion — is completely inappropriate.

This is not simply about a Discord profile picture.

It is about the standards used by the official community of a historical strategy game.

Hearts of Iron IV contains countless political leaders, ideologies and controversial historical figures. Yet a Turkish player can apparently be punished simply for displaying a photograph of the founder of the Republic of Türkiye, while moderators invoke disputed historical claims to justify that decision.

If Paradox wants to enforce rules regarding political figures, then those rules should be clear, consistent and applied equally. They should not be selectively used against one historical figure while the game itself extensively features political and military leaders from the same era.

Historical debate is perfectly legitimate. Distorting or oversimplifying history in order to justify moderation decisions is not.

I expect Paradox Interactive and the Hearts of Iron IV team to publicly address this incident, clarify what their actual policy is, and take responsibility for the statements made by their moderators.

This review is not about demanding special treatment for Turkish players. It is about demanding **consistent moderation, historical responsibility and basic respect for the community surrounding the game.**

TR: Tam 300 saatimi verdiğim Hearts of Iron IV ve Paradox Interactive, yıllardır süregelen sistematik çifte standartları ve Türk düşmanı tutumlarıyla benim için artık bitmiştir. Bugüne kadar bu firmaya harcadığım zamana ve paraya hayatımın en büyük pişmanlıklarından biri olarak bakıyorum.
Oyuncu kitlesinin büyüklüğüne rağmen yıllardır bir Türkçe dil desteğinin ısrarla çok görülmesi kesinlikle tesadüf değildir. Adı "Battle for the Bosphorus" olan ve Türkiye'yi merkeze alan bir DLC çıkarıp, içine tek bir TSK marşı, Mehter veya en basitinden Türk temalı bir profil ikonu bile koymamaları bu vizyonsuzluğun ve art niyetin açık bir özetidir. Irak gibi bölgelere gerçeklikle uzaktan yakından ilgisi olmayan fantastik rotalar eklenirken, tarihsel bir gerçekliği olan Doğu Türkistan'ın oyunda esamesinin bile okunmaması, firmanın olaylara ne kadar politik ve taraflı yaklaştığını kanıtlamaktadır.
Tüm bu ayrımcı oyun tasarımları bir yana, bardağı taşıran son damla resmi kanallardaki zehirli topluluk yönetimidir. Yetkilendirilmiş bir Discord moderatörünün Cumhuriyetimizin kurucusu Gazi Mustafa Kemal Atatürk’e ve atalarımıza yönelik yaptığı hadsiz, soykırımcı benzetmeler asla kabul edilemez. Kendi projelerini üreten bir oyun geliştiricisi olarak topluluk yönetiminin ne kadar hassas bir konu olduğunu çok iyi biliyorum; yetkili konumdaki bir şahsın bu denli nefret dolu bir söylemde bulunup anında ihraç edilmemesi basit bir ihmal değil, bilinçli bir göz yummadır. Aynı ırkçı ve düşmanca tavır, kendini sürekli kurban rolünde gösteren başka bir millete yapılsaydı yaptırımların ne kadar acımasız ve hızlı olacağını hepimiz çok iyi biliyoruz.
Bu ikiyüzlü politikalar son bulana, bahsi geçen nefret söylemlerine karşı kalıcı yaptırımlar uygulanana ve oyun içi negatif ayrımcılıklar giderilene kadar Paradox Interactive'e ait hiçbir oyunu oynamama ve satın almama kararı aldım. Türk milletine, tarihine ve milli değerlerine gönül bağı olan herkesi bu çifte standarda karşı durmaya ve boykota davet ediyorum.

EN: Having dedicated a full 300 hours to Hearts of Iron IV and Paradox Interactive, I am entirely done with this company due to its long-standing double standards and anti-Turkish stance. Looking back, I consider the time and money I spent on this studio one of the greatest regrets of my life.
The persistent refusal to provide Turkish language support over the years—despite the massive size of the local player base—is certainly no coincidence. Releasing a DLC titled "Battle for the Bosphorus," explicitly centered on Turkey, without including even a single Turkish Armed Forces march, Mehter anthem, or the simplest Turkish-themed profile icon clearly epitomizes this lack of vision and malicious intent. Furthermore, while completely ahistorical and fantasy paths are added to regions like Iraq, East Turkestan—a nation with concrete historical existence—is not even acknowledged, proving just how politically motivated and biased the studio's design choices are.
Beyond these discriminatory in-game elements, the final straw has been the toxic moderation across their official channels. The insolent, genocidal comparisons directed at Gazi Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the founder of our Republic, and our ancestors by an authorized Discord moderator are entirely unacceptable. As an indie game developer myself, I know firsthand how critical community management is; allowing an individual in a position of authority to spread such hateful rhetoric without being immediately removed is not mere negligence, but conscious complicity. We all know full well that if this same hostile, discriminatory attitude had been directed toward nations that constantly portray themselves as victims, the retaliation and penalties would have been swift and uncompromising.
Until these hypocritical policies come to an end, lasting disciplinary action is taken against such hate speech, and in-game prejudices are corrected, I have decided to boycott Paradox Interactive entirely by refusing to play or purchase any of their games. I call upon everyone who feels a bond of heart to the Turkish nation, its history, and its national values to stand against this blatant double standard and join this boycott.

This is not about the game. It is about how Paradox’s official HOI4 Discord treated Turkish players.

A player was banned for using a historical photograph of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk as a profile picture. The moderator called Atatürk “controversial and polarizing,” compared him to Karl Marx, and tied him to the events of 1915 through the Committee of Union and Progress. In 1915 Atatürk was a frontline officer at Gallipoli, not the official running Ottoman central policy. The Republic of Türkiye was founded in 1923.

The same community allows portraits of far more contested 20th-century leaders. The in-game Atatürk portrait is permitted; a real historical photograph is not. Players who objected had messages removed and were banned. The Discord was then closed to new joins.

That is a double standard, not moderation. Paradox sells Turkish content and a Turkey DLC while its official community treats the founder of the modern Turkish state as something to be sanitized off a profile picture.

Correct the record, apply the same rule to every historical figure, and apologize. Until then I cannot recommend this game or Paradox’s community management.

I am writing this review because I strongly object to the disrespectful and historically misleading way Mustafa Kemal Atatürk and the Turkish people are portrayed in Hearts of Iron IV.

Historical subjects such as the events of 1915 are extremely sensitive and remain disputed. However, presenting Atatürk as someone who personally carried out an “Armenian genocide” in 1915 is historically misleading. The events of 1915 took place during the Ottoman Empire and before the establishment of the Republic of Türkiye. Atatürk should not simply be portrayed as the person responsible for events in which he was not the governing authority.

You are free to represent controversial historical events and different interpretations in your game, but that does not justify portraying a historical figure or an entire nation in a deliberately insulting or one-sided manner.

Atatürk is the founder of the Republic of Türkiye and is an extremely important historical figure to millions of Turkish people. Criticism of historical figures is legitimate, but there is a clear difference between historical criticism and disrespectful or defamatory representation.

I am asking Paradox Interactive to review this content and correct any historically inaccurate or unnecessarily offensive portrayal of Atatürk and the Turkish people.

We are asking for basic historical accuracy and respect, not special treatment.

If this issue is not addressed, many Turkish players may reconsider purchasing DLCs or continuing to support the game, and some may choose to request refunds for their purchases.

I hope Paradox will approach this issue seriously, review the relevant content, and provide an appropriate correction and apology to Turkish players.

Historical games have a responsibility to treat history carefully, especially when dealing with subjects that still have a profound impact on millions of people.

I have enjoyed Hearts of Iron IV for a long time, but I cannot recommend it while Paradox tolerates what happened on its official Discord server.

A Turkish player was banned simply for using a portrait of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk as a profile picture. A moderator justified this by claiming Atatürk was a CUP member "during the Armenian genocide" and that his role was "debatable." This is a distortion of history.

The facts: Atatürk joined the Committee of Union and Progress in 1907, but by 1909 he had openly clashed with its leadership and distanced himself from its politics. In 1915 he was not in Istanbul making decisions; he was a divisional commander at Gallipoli, defending his country against an invasion. He had no role in the policies of 1915. Linking him to those events is not "debate," it is slander.

Atatürk founded the modern Republic of Turkey, gave women the right to vote and be elected earlier than many European countries, and built his foreign policy on the principle "Peace at home, peace in the world." Even his former enemies respected him: the Anzac memorial at Gallipoli carries his famous words of reconciliation toward the fallen soldiers of the countries that invaded Turkey. Using such a figure as a political tool is shameful.

As Turks, we believe the 1915 events are presented one-sidedly, and that the genocide label is a politically motivated claim that ignores the suffering of Turks and Muslims. Throughout modern history, Turks have far more often been victims of massacres and expulsions than perpetrators: millions of Muslims and Turks were killed or driven from the Balkans, the Caucasus and Crimea in the 19th and early 20th centuries, and Turkish civilians in Eastern Anatolia also suffered massacres during the same war. None of this is ever mentioned when our history is judged.

This is not only about history. No one should face racism or discrimination in a community server because of their nationality or their nation's founder. Other players are free to display their own national figures; Turkish players should be treated the same way.

Hearts of Iron IV has one of its largest player bases in Turkey. Paradox should:

Publicly apologize to the Turkish community.
Lift the bans on the affected players.
Take appropriate action against the moderators responsible.
Ensure its community rules are applied equally, without nationality-based double standards.

No historical figure should be distorted, and no player should be discriminated against. I will change this review when Paradox corrects this mistake.

The way Paradox is handling users who use Atatürk as their profile picture is deeply concerning. Penalizing players simply for using the image of a historical figure, and then justifying it by describing Atatürk as a “controversial figure,” is an unacceptable approach to moderation.

Even more troubling are the responses reportedly given to appeals, which bring Atatürk, the Committee of Union and Progress, and the Armenian Genocide into the justification. This is an extremely sensitive and historically contested subject, and using such a characterization as a basis for moderating a player’s profile picture is highly inappropriate.

Unless a profile picture is being used to harass, threaten, or promote hatred against others, why should it be a moderation issue at all? Players should be allowed to express their historical and political interests without Paradox deciding which historical figures are “acceptable” to display.

As someone who has enjoyed Paradox games, I find this approach extremely disappointing and hope the company reconsiders how it applies its moderation policies.

I have spent over 900 hours playing Hearts of Iron IV, and that alone should show how much time, patience, and money I have invested into this title. But looking past the surface, the technical state of the game has simply become unacceptable. The optimization is terrible, with late-game performance slowing down to an unplayable crawl after 1942 regardless of your hardware. At this point, the modding community is practically carrying the entire game on its back, delivering actual depth, balance, and quality content for free while Paradox does the bare minimum. Instead of fixing core mechanics or engine bottlenecks, Paradox continues its predatory monetization model, carving out basic quality-of-life features and meager focus trees just to sell them back to us through overpriced DLCs.

On top of these ongoing technical frustrations, I am changing my recommendation because of the recent moderation controversy in the official Hearts of Iron community.

Turkish players have raised serious concerns regarding moderation involving Mustafa Kemal Atatürk and other Turkish historical figures. What made the situation particularly disturbing was not simply the enforcement of a profile-picture rule, but the reported justification: Atatürk was characterized as a “controversial and polarizing” figure, while disputed claims concerning the events of 1915 were brought into the moderation process.

There were also reports of inconsistent enforcement. While Turkish historical figures were being targeted, users displaying figures such as Hitler and Stalin were reportedly still present, with action against some of them appearing only after Turkish players began pointing out the inconsistency.

Atatürk is the founder of the Republic of Türkiye and holds profound historical importance for Turkish people. That does not mean he, or any historical figure, should be immune from legitimate historical discussion or criticism. But historical debate and apparently selective community moderation based on disputed historical accusations are two very different things.

And this is not something I can simply dismiss as “one Discord moderator.” This happened in an official community operating under the Hearts of Iron and Paradox name. Whether moderators are employees, contractors or volunteers, Paradox is responsible for the standards maintained in its official communities.

Turkish players have supported Hearts of Iron IV for years. We buy the overpriced DLCs, endure broken late-game performance, spend thousands of hours playing it, and form a substantial part of its community. We are not asking for special treatment. We are asking for consistent rules, actual technical support, and basic respect.

After 900+ hours, leaving a negative review is not something I do lightly. I loved this game, and that is precisely why I care about this.

Until Paradox properly investigates what happened, addresses the inconsistent moderation, respects its player base, and finally fixes the state of the game, I cannot recommend Hearts of Iron IV.
